Acceptance of the FY 2025-26 Pavement Rehabilitation Project (CS26A). Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301 (c) of the CEQA Guidelines. This section exempts projects characterized as minor alterations to public facilities involving negligible or no expansion of the existing site. Maintenance and repair are proposed on existing public streets but do not create additional automobile lanes. The proposed project meets the criteria for this exemption. Contact Person: Engineer I Esteller
1) Authorize the filing of the Notice of Completion for the subject project; 2) Authorize the release of the Payment Bond in full upon the recording of the Notice of Completion; 3) Authorize the release of the Performance Bond in full one (1) year after the recording of the Notice of Completion; and 4) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2026-74, titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Accepting the FY 2025-26 Pavement Rehabilitation Project (CS26A)".

10D.
Approve the Design for the Park Equipment Replacement at Wiro and Orpheus Parks Project (CP23D) and Authorize Advertisement for Construction. Environmental Considerations: There are separate environmental considerations for Wiro Park and Orpheus Park.
Wiro Park:
The proposed project is exempt under State CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 - Existing Facilities, which is a Class 1 exemption. Class 1 exemptions, "consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of existing or former use". Additionally, the proposed project is exempt under State CEQA Guidelines Section 15302 - Replacement or Reconstruction, which is a Class 2 exemption. Class 2 exemptions, "consists of replacement or reconstruction of existing structures and facilities where the new structure will be located on the same site as the structure replaced and will have substantially the same purpose and capacity as the structure replaced". Furthermore, within State CEQA Guidelines Section 15302, CEQA Guidelines Section 15302(b) would apply, for the "replacement of a commercial structure with a new structure of substantially the same size, purpose and capacity". The proposed project consists of a request for approval of a Substantial Conformance Permit for the removal and replacement of existing playground equipment, safety surfacing and drainage improvements for the existing community park.
Orpheus Park:
The proposed project is exempt under State CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 - Existing Facilities, which is a Class 1 exemption. Class 1 exemptions, "consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of existing or former use". Additionally, the proposed project is exempt under State CEQA Guidelines Section 15302 - Replacement or Reconstruction, which is a Class 2 exemption. Class 2 exemptions, "consists of replacement or reconstruction of existing structures and facilities where the new structure will be located on the same site as the structure replaced and will have substantially the same purpose and capacity as the structure replaced". The proposed scope of work includes the removal and replacement of existing playground equipment, safety surfacing and drainage improvements for the existing community park. Contact Person: Engineer I DeWhite
1) Approve the design and plans for the Park Equipment Replacement at Wiro and Orpheus Parks Project (CP23D); 2) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2026-73 titled, "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Approving the Design and Plans for Construction of the Park Equipment Replacement at Wiro and Orpheus Parks Project (CP23D), Pursuant to Government Code Section 830.6"; and 3) Authorize the advertisement of the Park Equipment Replacement at Wiro and Orpheus Parks Project (CP23D) for construction bids.

Authorization to award a Construction Contract to Nu Line Technologies, LLC for the FY 2026-27 Drainage Rehabilitation Project (CD27A) and Lake Drive Storm Drain Lining Project (CD27B). Environmental Considerations: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Environmental Initial Study (IS) was conducted for the Lake Drive Storm Drain Project, which determined that the proposed project may have potentially significant environmental effects related to biological resources, geology and soils, cultural resources, and tribal cultural resources. Specific mitigation measures were determined to avoid or mitigate the potential significant environmental impacts to below established levels of significance. A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) was prepared and adopted by the Planning Commission (PC Resolution No. 2026-15). A Notice of Determination was filed with the State Clearing House (SCH#2025110169) and County Clerk Office (2026-000567). All mitigation measures applicable to the Lake Drive Storm Drain Lining Project will be implemented.
The FY 2026-27 Drainage Rehabilitation Project is Categorically Exempt (CE) from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15302 (c) of the CEQA Guidelines. This section exempts the replacement and reconstruction of existing facilities that will substantially have the same purpose and capacity as the structure being replaced. None of the exceptions in Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines are applicable to the project. Contact Person: Engineer I Estellar
1) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, in consultation with the City Attorney, to execute a construction contract agreement in substantial form, with Nu Line Technologies, LLC and any necessary amendments and time extensions in the amount of $1,091,500 plus a contingency of $163,725 for a total not-to-exceed construction contract amount of $1,255,225 to construct the Base Bid only; and 2) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2026-88, titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Amending the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget".

14A.
Council Initiated Item by Deputy Mayor O'Hara: Direct City Manager's Office to include official city participation in International Dark Sky Week 2027 (April 12-19, 2027) as part of the 2027 calendar.
Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15378(b)(5) of CEQA Guidelines. The action involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
Direct the City Manager's Office to explore and organize the City's Staff/Facilities and its partners to participate in International Dark Skies Week in the following capacities; City Facilities & Lighting Controls
Municipal Dimmings & Audits: Turn off non-essential architectural and exterior lighting at City Hall, community parks, and administrative facilities after 9:00 PM during the week of April 12-19, 2027. Streetlight Policy Alignment: Request Public Works conduct a review of existing municipal fixtures to prioritize full-cutoff, warm-spectrum (2700K or lower) LED retrofits along sensitive ecological borders.
Community & Astronomy Events
Lagoon & Beach Stargazing Nights: Partner with the San Elijo Lagoon Ecological Reserve and local astronomy organizations (such as the San Diego Astronomy Association) to host guided telescope viewings and nocturnal wildlife walks.
Encinitas Library Public or Community Center Workshops:
Host educational presentations on dark sky preservation, home lighting fixture retrofits, and night sky photography.
Public Education & Business Engagement
Dark Sky Business Recognition: Partner with MainStreet Associations (Downtown Encinitas, Leucadia, Cardiff, Chamber of Commerce) through their annual MOU to encourage downtown merchants to turn off decorative storefront signage after closing.
Residential "Lights Out" Campaign: Launch a public outreach campaign encouraging residents to shield exterior fixtures, direct outdoor lights downward, and utilize motion sensors or timers.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
